```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 15_related_anova_columns_and_rows
title: Columns and rows
questions:
  - id: columns_and_rows_reflection
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Save response
    prompt: >
      Before we go on, think about why the scores differ within each kind of
      group. Looking down a column, why might the five times differ from one
      another? Looking along a row, why might one child's three times differ?
      Which of those reasons do we care about for our question about practice
      and competition?
    explanation: >
      There isn't a single response to mark right or wrong here. But notice
      that the two groupings point to different reasons. Down a column, we have
      five different children in the same race, and much of the spread comes
      from some kids just being faster than others. Along a row, it's the same
      child every time, so their overall speed can't be the reason the times
      differ. What changes is the race: more practice, a rival, or just a
      better or worse run. Keep that in mind. Grouping the same scores in
      different ways is how we're going to pull those sources of variability
      apart.
```
